objection.quote: Observe that the mass \(2^n-\mu\) together with all pieces of \(P\) may be viewed as a subdivision of a stick of length \(2^n-\mu+\sum P=S_n-\mu\le S_{n-1}\) performed with at most \(m+(k-1)\le n-1\) cuts.
objection.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the asserted inequality S_n - mu <= S_{n-1}, which only requires mu > tau = 2^{n-1}. Take n = 2, so B_2 = {1,2,4}, S_2 = 7, S_1 = 3, tau = 2. Use t = 1 <= n cut, placed inside the bin of length 4 at distance 3.5, so k = 1, m = 0, P = {1,2}, Q = {3.5,0.5}, mu = 3.5 > tau = 2 (subcase hypothesis holds). Then S_n - mu = 7 - 3.5 = 3.5 > 3 = S_1, contradicting the claimed bound. Consequently the dummy piece of length S_{n-1} - (S_n - mu) = -0.5 has negative length and the ensuing appeal to the inductive hypothesis on a padded copy of B_{n-1} is vacuous. (The text also silently identifies this dummy length with d = mu - tau, whereas S_{n-1}-(S_n-mu) = mu - 2^n, a different quantity.)
objection.load_bearing: The whole k>=1, mu>tau subcase derives D(M)>=1 from applying the induction hypothesis to the padded remainder; with the padding step invalid the subcase has no proof, and the remaining text there ('something that forces', 'the worst case', numerical checks for n<=3) supplies no substitute.
